player_0.content: New plan: I incorrectly assumed that because Traffic is a confounder, simply observing the total correlation (Method 2) is insufficient or biased, without explicitly verifying the independence assumption between the confounder (Traffic) and the treatment (Solar Eclipse). The problem states the world has "only the following conditions" and "no unmentioned factors," which implies Traffic and Solar Eclipse are independent. Therefore, Method 2 (general correlation) actually yields the correct causal effect because there is no backdoor path to block. Method 1 (conditioning) is unnecessary and potentially problematic if it implies a causal link between the two independent causes. My strategy failed because I misidentified the necessity of adjustment in a world with no hidden confounders. Next time, I will first check if the confounder is independent of the treatment; if they are independent, I will conclude that Method 2 is correct and answer "No" to whether Method 1 is better.
